### 1.  What does the condition on triples mean?

Consider three teams \(A,B,C\) and the three games among them.

*If the three games are all draws* then each team gets  
\(1+1=2\) points – all three totals are equal.

*If the three games are decisive* then each team gets either
\(2+0=2\) (one win, one loss) or \(0+0=0\) or \(2+2=4\).  
The only way the three totals are equal is when each team has one win
and one loss, i.e. the three directed edges form a **directed 3‑cycle**.

Thus the statement  

> “any three teams scored a pair of different points among themselves”

is equivalent to saying that **no triple of vertices can be

* a triangle whose three edges are all draws, **or**
* a triangle whose three edges are all directed and form a directed cycle.**

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 2.  Consequences for the colouring

*If a triangle of draws existed*, the condition would be violated,
so the red (draw) subgraph must contain **no triangle**.  
Hence the set of draw edges forms a *triangle‑free* graph on \(N\) vertices.

*If a triangle of directed edges existed*, it would have to be a
directed cycle, which is also forbidden.  
We can avoid this simply by imposing a **linear order** on the teams and
orienting every non‑draw edge from the higher‑ranked team to the lower‑ranked one.
In that case any triangle that uses only directed edges is transitive,
so no directed 3‑cycle occurs.  
Therefore the only real restriction is the triangle‑free condition on draws.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 3.  Maximum possible number of draws

The classic Turán theorem tells us that a triangle‑free graph on \(N\) vertices
has at most  

\[
\operatorname{ex}(N,K_3)=\Big\lfloor\frac{N^{2}}{4}\Big\rfloor
\]

edges, and this bound is attained by a complete bipartite graph with parts
of sizes \(\lfloor N/2\rfloor\) and \(\lceil N/2\rceil\).

Hence

\[
D_{\max}\le \Big\lfloor\frac{N^{2}}{4}\Big\rfloor .
\]

### 4.  Construction that reaches the bound

Divide the teams into two groups  

\[
A,\;|A|=\big\lfloor N/2\big\rfloor ,\qquad
B,\;|B|=\big\lceil N/2\big\rceil .
\]

* For every pair \((a,b)\) with \(a\in A,\;b\in B\) make the game a **draw**.
  This yields \(|A|\cdot|B|=\big\lfloor N^{2}/4\big\rfloor\) draws.
* Within each group orient the games consistently with a ranking
  (e.g. higher index beats lower).  Thus all intra‑group edges are decisive,
  and any triangle that lies completely inside one group is transitive,
  never a directed 3‑cycle.

Now any three teams contain either
* two teams from the same group (giving at least one decisive edge), or
* one team from each group together with a second team from either group;
  in either case not all three edges are draws.

Consequently the required condition on triples is satisfied, and we have
exactly \(\lfloor N^{2}/4\rfloor\) draws.
